Job Title: Software Engineer (Electron.js)


Job Type: Full-time


Location: Remote


The Role

We’re building high-fidelity productivity infrastructure for a globally distributed workforce—software that operates quietly, reliably, and intelligently in the background. As a Software Engineer focused on desktop systems, you’ll help design and scale a cross-platform time intelligence application (MacOS + Windows) used daily by thousands of professionals.


What You’ll Work On

  1. Architect and evolve a cross-platform desktop agent using Electron.js, optimized for performance and minimal resource footprint.
  2. Build real-time timekeeping systems with precise event tracking and background execution.
  3. Design and implement system-level signal collection (keyboard, mouse, app usage) with strong privacy and efficiency guarantees.
  4. Develop offline-first data pipelines with reliable background sync and conflict resolution.
  5. Integrate with distributed backend services and internal APIs to enable analytics and reporting.
  6. Continuously improve runtime performance, memory efficiency, and fault tolerance.
  7. Collaborate with product, design, and backend teams to ship features that directly impact user productivity.


What We're Looking For

  1. 3+ years building production-grade desktop applications with Electron.js.
  2. Strong proficiency in JavaScript/TypeScript and Node.js.
  3. Experience designing cross-platform systems (MacOS + Windows) with consistent behavior.
  4. Hands-on work with real-time tracking, event streams, or activity monitoring systems.
  5. Familiarity with OS-level APIs for capturing user/system interactions.
  6. Deep understanding of performance optimization in desktop environments.
  7. Strong debugging skills and ability to reason about edge cases in distributed/offline systems.


Preferred

  1. Experience building productivity, monitoring, or telemetry-driven applications.
  2. Knowledge of native OS integrations (permissions, background processes, system hooks).
  3. Understanding of security and privacy considerations in user activity tracking.
  4. Familiarity with auto-update systems and release management in Electron.

You'll work across cloud infrastructure, deployment systems, monitoring, security, and incident response, building the tools and workflows that allow a small engineering team to move exceptionally fast without compromising reliability.


We're looking for someone who has operated complex production systems, understands infrastructure at a deep level, and is already using AI coding agents to fundamentally change how engineering work gets done.


What You'll Do

  1. Build agentic infrastructure: Design and implement AI-powered workflows for infrastructure provisioning, deployments, monitoring, incident detection, and automated remediation.
  2. Own reliability at scale: Architect resilient, secure, and scalable cloud infrastructure that supports rapidly evolving AI products and workloads.
  3. Make systems observable: Build comprehensive logging, metrics, distributed tracing, and alerting systems that provide actionable visibility into production health.
  4. Automate operational complexity: Eliminate repetitive infrastructure work through intelligent automation, self-service tooling, and agent-driven operations.
  5. Own infrastructure lifecycle management: Drive cloud security hygiene, dependency upgrades, runtime migrations, and infrastructure modernization from design through production.
  6. Improve developer velocity: Build infrastructure platforms and workflows that make deploying, debugging, and operating services effortless for engineers.
  7. Raise the engineering bar: Mentor engineers, establish technical standards, and influence architectural decisions through hands-on technical leadership.


What We're Looking For

  1. Staff-level engineering expertise with deep experience in Infrastructure, DevOps, Site Reliability Engineering, or Platform Engineering.
  2. Strong hands-on experience operating production systems on major cloud platforms such as AWS, GCP, or Azure.
  3. Expertise in infrastructure as code, container orchestration, CI/CD, networking, cloud security, and distributed systems.
  4. Demonstrated experience designing observability and incident response systems for complex production environments.
  5. Proven ownership of infrastructure migrations, security improvements, and reliability initiatives.
  6. AI-native engineering habits: You already use AI coding agents extensively in your daily development workflow and have built automation that meaningfully reduces engineering toil.
  7. Strong software engineering fundamentals and the ability to build internal tools, automation frameworks, and production-grade infrastructure services.
  8. A track record of independently identifying systemic problems, designing solutions, and shipping them end to end.
  9. Experience mentoring engineers and improving technical practices while remaining deeply involved in implementation.


Nice to have

  1. You've built infrastructure automation that eliminates entire categories of manual operational work.
  2. You've experimented with or deployed AI agents for infrastructure operations, incident triage, or automated remediation.
  3. You think about infrastructure as a programmable, increasingly autonomous system rather than a collection of manually managed services.
  4. You've helped small engineering teams operate highly reliable systems at significant scale.
  5. You're equally comfortable debugging a production incident, designing infrastructure architecture, and writing the code to improve both.


Compensation & Benefits Notice

The national pay range for this full-time position is base salary of $220,000 –$300,000. All employees are eligible for equity compensation, and employees may also receive performance-based bonuses, dependent on role and subject to company policies. micro1 provides a comprehensive benefits package, including up to 100% reimbursement for health-insurance premiums, paid time off, a 401(K) plan with a company match, and additional benefits designed to support a high-performing, remote-first workforce.


micro1 is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable local laws, regulations and ordinances. If you need assistance and/or a reasonable accommodation during the application process, reach out to support@micro1.ai.


Our hiring process utilizes artificial intelligence tools to assist in candidate screening and assessment. Our AI tools are designed to complement, not replace, human decision-making.

Role Title: Bluebook Citation Specialist (Law Students & Recent JDs)


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


Opportunity Snapshot


Pay: $50–80/hour

You’ll need: Current or recent law school enrollment, hands-on Bluebook experience, and law journal or law review editing experience

Your tasks: Review citation-checking rubrics and build sample cite-checking tasks


Job Description

micro1 is engaging law students and recent law graduates with law journal experience to support a legal citation project. If you’ve spent time cite-checking for a law review or journal, this is that skill applied to a new context. No prior AI experience is required — your Bluebook fluency and editorial judgment are what matter.


Scope of Work

  1. Review existing Bluebook and pincite grading rubrics, and flag rules that are unclear, incomplete, or would be applied inconsistently by different editors.
  2. Identify edge cases the rubrics don’t currently cover and recommend how they should be handled.
  3. Create sample cite-checking tasks: source material paired with citations containing realistic errors, along with the correct answer and an explanation of the rule involved.
  4. Build tasks across a range of citation types and difficulty levels, from straightforward formatting errors to subtle pincite and source-support problems.
  5. Apply Bluebook rules consistently across all submissions.
  6. Flag ambiguous cases to project coordinators instead of resolving them silently.
  7. Deliver assigned work on schedule and at the required quality level.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Current law student (2L, 3L) or recent JD graduate.
  2. Law review or law journal experience, ideally including a cite-checking or source-collection role.
  3. Strong working knowledge of The Bluebook, including pincites, short forms, signals, and parentheticals.
  4. Able to explain why a citation is wrong, not just that it is — the reasoning matters as much as the correction.
  5. Careful and consistent across long sessions of detailed review work.
  6. Comfortable working independently and meeting deadlines without close supervision.
  7. Experience as a journal editor, articles editor, or executive editor is a plus.


How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview— this is how we showcase your skills to the client
  3. Profile review by the hiring team
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Job Title: Forward Deployed Engineer, U.S. Government


Job Type: Full-time


Location: Remote (requires relocating to DC area)


The Role

We’re hiring an MTS to work on applied AI systems across research and production. This role spans model experimentation, infrastructure, and deployment in high-assurance, mission-critical environments, including forward-deployed work with strategic partners to ensure mission success.


What You’ll Work On

  1. Build and deploy agentic AI systems that support high-impact U.S. Government missions from prototype to production.
  2. Design and integrate LLM applications, including multi-agent systems, tool-using agents, RAG workflows, and human-in-the-loop autonomy.
  3. Work directly with government partners in forward-deployed environments to translate mission needs into technical systems.
  4. Build and maintain large-scale data curation, and evaluation pipelines for model training and improvement.
  5. Develop infrastructure for model inference, experimentation, evaluation, and deployment across frontier AI platforms.
  6. Build AI systems that turn mission data, models, and tools into real operational autonomy.
  7. Own systems across the full lifecycle, including discovery, architecture, implementation, deployment, reliability, security, and iteration.


What We're Looking For

  1. Able to operate independently in ambiguous, partner-facing settings with technical and operational ownership.
  2. Strong Python engineer with end-to-end ownership experience.
  3. Experience with LLMs and creating agentic systems.
  4. Built or maintained data pipelines / ML infrastructure.
  5. Familiar with RL workflows or simulation environments.
  6. Comfortable in high-security / high-reliability environments.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Active U.S. security clearance or eligibility and willingness to obtain one.
  2. Experience supporting U.S. Government, defense, intelligence, or national security missions.
  3. Prior experience at a startup, defense organization, Department of War, or government-focused technology company.
  4. Background operating in fast-moving startup environments, mission-critical government settings, or both.


Compensation & Benefits Notice

The national pay range for this full-time position is base salary of $150,000 –$250,000. Role Title: AI Agent Evaluator

Role Type: Contractor

Location: U.S based


Opportunity Snapshot


Pay: $25-45/hour

Time per task: ~1.5 hours per run (evidence and scoring included)

Project kickoff: Monday, October 12

Onboarding: Today (Fri), Saturday, or Sunday, so you’re ready to start Monday October 10th

You’ll need: An active personal popular AI account (Free, Go, or Plus; not Pro), an active personal and a smartphone that can screen record

Your tasks: Run everyday errands with two AI agents, approve key steps, screen record, and score the results


About the role


AI agents are starting to handle real-life errands: paying bills, booking trips, doing the groceries. We want to know how well they actually do it, from the point of view of a real user. That’s you.

You’ll test two AI agents side by side, using your own accounts on your phone, and tell us what worked, what didn’t, and how it felt.


What you’ll do

  1. Run real-life scenarios: bills, returns, email follow-ups, bookings, shopping, groceries, travel, family logistics, outings, and forms
  2. Approve or stop the agent at key steps
  3. Screen record every attempt
  4. Score each run on completion, quality, control issues, satisfaction, and time
  5. Share clear written feedback on the agent experience

Who we’re looking for

  1. US-based, with a Bachelor’s degree
  2. Someone who already uses AI in daily life
  3. 2-3 years of experience, preferably in engineering, business management, or office/operations
  4. Detail-oriented, great at following instructions and documenting each step
  5. Clear written communication
  6. Generalists welcome, domain experts preferred
  7. No coding or AI background needed


Why you’ll like it

  1. Get paid to use the AI tools you already use
  2. Work entirely from your phone, on your schedule
  3. Have a direct say in how next-generation AI agents get built and improved


How the selection process works

  1. Apply
  2. Complete the screening questions
  3. Interview: 15-30 minutes max
  4. Profile review: if everything looks good, we present you to the client
  5. Onboarding: our Talent Ops team will contact you to get you started

Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is engaging Lawyer/Legal Writers to participate in an evaluation and analysis opportunity focused on advanced AI system development for a customer project. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. Job Title: VP of Robotics Research


Job Type: Full-time


Location: Remote


The Role

As VP of Robotics Research at micro1, you will define and lead our research agenda for Physical AI — intelligent systems that can understand, reason about, and act in the physical world.


Our research focuses on four connected areas:

  1. Physical Agents & Robotics — building agents that perceive, reason, plan, and act through robots, machines, instruments, and other physical systems.
  2. Learning & Data — studying how demonstrations, trajectories, sensor data, simulation, feedback, and autonomous experience improve physical-world intelligence.
  3. Evaluation & Generalization — developing rigorous methods to measure physical reasoning, manipulation, planning, robustness, safety, and transfer across tasks and environments.
  4. Physical-World R&D Automation — exploring how agents can accelerate scientific and engineering workflows through simulation, experimentation, design, fabrication, and real-world tools.


You will set research direction across these areas, stay close to models and physical systems, build a world-class research team, and partner with leading AI and robotics labs on their hardest Physical AI problems.


What You’ll Do

  1. Set the Physical AI research agenda. Identify the highest-leverage problems across robotics, embodied agents, learning, data, evaluation, and physical-world automation.
  2. Build agents that act in the physical world. Develop systems that connect foundation models and agents to robots, machines, instruments, and other physical interfaces.
  3. Advance general-purpose robot learning. Lead research across vision-language-action models, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, world models, and multimodal policies.
  4. Develop a science of physical-world data. Study which demonstrations, trajectories, sensor streams, environments, and supervision signals best improve learning and generalization.
  5. Build scalable data-generation systems. Develop methods for generating high-quality interaction data through human demonstration, teleoperation, autonomous rollout, simulation, and hybrid human–agent workflows.
  6. Advance evaluation and generalization. Build rigorous benchmarks for manipulation, spatial reasoning, planning, tool use, robustness, safety, and transfer across tasks and embodiments.
  7. Bridge simulation and reality. Study how simulated and real-world experience should be combined and where sim-to-real transfer breaks down.
  8. Advance physical-world R&D automation. Build agents that operate across scientific and engineering workflows, including simulation, experimentation, design, fabrication, and laboratory systems.
  9. Build research that compounds. Create reusable datasets, environments, simulators, hardware testbeds, evaluation infrastructure, and research tools.
  10. Build and lead the research team. Recruit and develop exceptional researchers and engineers, partner with leading labs, and publish consequential research.


What We’re Looking For

  1. Deep Physical AI expertise. Significant experience in robotics, embodied AI, robot learning, autonomous systems, or related fields.
  2. Strong learning and agentic systems intuition. Deep understanding of modern robot learning, multimodal models, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, world models, planning, and control.
  3. Physical systems intuition. Strong understanding of sensing, calibration, control, contact, actuation, latency, uncertainty, and hardware constraints.
  4. Exceptional research taste. You identify problems that can meaningfully expand what AI systems can do in the physical world.
  5. Experimental rigor. You turn open questions into strong hypotheses, controlled experiments, meaningful baselines, and evidence-backed conclusions.
  6. Strong evaluation judgment. You understand generalization, distribution shift, benchmark design, hardware-specific effects, and the failure modes of physical AI evaluations.
  7. Systems thinking. You reason across models, agents, data, hardware, simulation, tools, and evaluation as parts of a single system.
  8. Technical range. You are comfortable moving between model training, agent design, simulation, evaluation infrastructure, and physical experimentation.
  9. Research leadership. You have experience setting direction, mentoring exceptional technical talent, and leading ambitious research programs under uncertainty.


Preferred Qualifications

  1. Master’s or PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, AI, Machine Learning, Engineering, or a related field.
  2. Research experience at a leading AI, robotics, or embodied intelligence organization.
  3. Strong publication record at venues such as CoRL, RSS, ICRA, IROS, NeurIPS, ICML, or CVPR, or equivalent high-impact technical work.
  4. Experience with generalist robot policies, cross-embodiment learning, robot foundation models, or large-scale imitation and reinforcement learning.
  5. Hands-on experience with robotic platforms and frameworks such as ROS/ROS2, Isaac Lab, MuJoCo, ManiSkill, or equivalent systems.
  6. Experience building robotics benchmarks, simulation environments, teleoperation systems, safety evaluations, or physical-world data engines.
  7. Experience building agents for engineering, scientific, manufacturing, or laboratory workflows.

Role Title: Music & Sound Annotation Expert


Role Type: Contractor


Location: Remote


micro1 is engaging Music & Sound Annotation Experts to contribute to a customer's project at the forefront of music and audio technology.

Your ears are the ground truth. You'll listen to short field recordings and document exactly what's audible — instruments, tempo, key, background sounds, crowd reactions — through a structured web platform built for this project. Later phases involve grading AI model answers against what you actually heard.

  1. Listen to 30–90 second field recordings (headphones, your own quiet workspace) and complete structured annotations: which instruments are present, tempo and key, timestamps of background events (traffic, sirens, applause), scene details

  1. Working or gigging musicians, session players, producers, or mixing engineers
  2. Music educators, ear-training instructors, band/choir directors, conservatory students or graduates
  3. Location sound recordists, sound designers, foley artists, or podcast/documentary audio editors


Requirements

  1. 3+ years of hands-on music or audio experience
  2. Strong analytical listening: you can pick individual instruments out of a busy, noisy, real-world mix — not just studio recordings
  3. Can identify tempo (within a few BPM) and musical key (relative pitch with a reference is fine)
  4. Comfortable with detail-oriented, repetitive annotation work in a web platform — dropdowns, timestamps, short structured notes
  5. Clear written English for brief, evidence-based notes (e.g., "accordion enters around 0:12")
  6. Quality headphones, quiet workspace, reliable internet
  7. Available 20–25 hrs/week for the engagement window
